skill.name: security-audit
skill.description: Review code for common OWASP vulnerabilities, including injection, unsafe exception handling, path traversal, hardcoded secrets, and cross-site scripting.
skill.summary: Guide focused security reviews with vulnerable examples, safer patterns, severity guidance, and practical remediation.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by educational Markdown, detection regular expressions, and intentionally vulnerable examples. The audit confirms a predictable API key fallback and finds missing shell-injection guidance plus active testing instructions without authorization controls.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the default credential. Require the variable, or enforce a development-only guard that cannot run in production.
Add the referenced cookbook with safe command APIs, validation guidance, and framework examples, or remove the mandatory reference.
Require explicit user approval and written target authorization before sqlmap. Default to passive source review and explain possible service impact.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Shell-Injection Cookbook
semantic_findings.description: The workflow requires a shell-injection cookbook that is absent from the package. Reviews following this branch cannot load the promised detailed guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly references the relative cookbook, while the audited package contains only the SQL injection and bare-except cookbooks.

semantic_findings.title: Active SQL Testing Lacks Authorization Controls
semantic_findings.description: The automated testing guidance recommends database enumeration with sqlmap but does not require target authorization, scope confirmation, or user approval before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The active sqlmap command and database-enumeration option are explicit. Its localhost example limits the default reach, but the guidance lacks a safety boundary.

content.user_title: Audit Code for Common Security Vulnerabilities
content.value_statement: Security flaws can hide in queries, shell calls, file paths, exception handlers, and rendered output. This skill guides focused reviews and practical remediation across Python and TypeScript.
actual_capabilities: Reviews code for SQL injection, shell injection, path traversal, hardcoded secrets, cross-site scripting, and broad exception handling.
Compares vulnerable database operations with parameterized queries and ORM alternatives.
Explains safer Python exception handling with specific exceptions, logging, chaining, and re-raising.
Provides detection patterns for Python and TypeScript security reviews.
Produces severity-ranked findings with locations and remediation guidance.
limitations: Pattern-based review cannot prove that a codebase is free of vulnerabilities.
Examples focus mainly on Python and TypeScript, with limited framework-specific analysis.
The skill does not include a runnable scanner, so results depend on the files and context provided.
The referenced shell-injection cookbook is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Review a backend change
use_cases.description: Check new database, file, and command-handling code before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Triage security findings
use_cases.description: Classify likely vulnerabilities, explain impact, and propose specific remediations for review.

use_cases.title: Add a release security check
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist to sensitive changes before deployment approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review one file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file for common security flaws. Explain each finding, assign severity, cite its location, and suggest a safer approach.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused review of one source file.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the files for this feature. Focus on trust boundaries, database queries, shell calls, paths, secrets, output encoding, and exception handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a small feature across several files.

prompt_templates.title: Validate reported findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these security findings against framework behavior and data flow. Separate confirmed vulnerabilities from false positives, then prioritize concrete fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Triage output from a scanner or earlier review.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a threat-driven audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Map entry points, untrusted inputs, privileged operations, and sensitive data flows. Audit each path, rank exploitability, and propose layered remediation with verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Conduct an advanced review of a security-sensitive subsystem.

output_examples.input: Review the user lookup flow for SQL injection.
output: High: A user identifier is inserted directly into a database query.
Use a parameterized query supported by the database driver.
Add a test with hostile input and verify the query structure remains unchanged.
Medium: The handler catches every exception and suppresses the failure.
Catch the narrowest expected exceptions and preserve unexpected failures.
Log useful context without exposing sensitive values.

output_examples.input: Audit a command that searches application logs.
output: Critical: Untrusted text reaches a shell command.
Use a list-form process API without a shell.
Validate the input and test shell metacharacters as hostile cases.

best_practices: Provide the relevant source files, framework versions, trust boundaries, and expected data flow.
Confirm framework-specific escaping and parameterization behavior before accepting or dismissing a finding.
Review high-impact findings manually and test each remediation against realistic hostile input.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every regular-expression match as a confirmed vulnerability.
Do not run active scanners against any target without explicit approval and authorization.
Do not include live credentials, tokens, or sensitive customer data in prompts or reports.

faq.question: Does this skill execute a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance, detection patterns, examples, and remediation advice.

faq.question: Which languages receive the strongest coverage?
faq.answer: Python and TypeScript receive the most detailed examples. General principles can support other languages.

faq.question: Can it detect every OWASP vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It covers several common patterns, but complete assurance requires architecture review, testing, and specialized tools.

faq.question: Will it distinguish safe framework features from unsafe interpolation?
faq.answer: It can use surrounding context, but framework versions and exact APIs must be provided for reliable adjudication.

faq.question: Can I use the output as a release gate?
faq.answer: Use it as one review input. Confirm important findings and verify remediations before making release decisions.

faq.question: How should active security tests be handled?
faq.answer: Obtain explicit approval, confirm written authorization, limit the target scope, and assess possible service impact before execution.
